editorial:
Imagine going on a relaxing weekend trip with your best friends, only to find out you are trapped behind three locked gates with hundreds of creepy deer just staring at you. That is exactly what happens to Hadria. She is already feeling bad about things she cannot quite remember, and the vibe at this lakeside spot is weird from the start. You get to know the group quickly, including the athletic Mike and the strange owners, Rick and Anna. The whole place feels off, especially when the owner, Bartleby, starts talking about the lake having the genes of gods. It sounds like a fake campfire story at first, but you will feel the tension build as the water starts acting very strange.

What really works here is how the movie keeps you guessing. The acting is solid, and the way the mystery unfolds makes it hard to look away. While the middle part slows down a bit, the payoff is totally worth it. If you love a good mix of sci-fi and scares, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the end, you find out the lake actually holds an ancient, living organism that can rewrite DNA. The twist is that Bartleby was using the guests as hosts to bring these god-like creatures back to life. Hadria discovers her missing memories were erased because she was a previous test subject. She manages to destroy the main hive in the water, but the movie ends with a hint that some of the creatures escaped into the wild.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves creature features and psychological mysteries.
